graphEvents.label: Does model and effort carry across the relaunch
The OpenCode plugin never records a model or effort
effort_is_valid and append_effort_arguments have no opencode case
OpenCode 2 relaunch drops the model flag by design
Pi carries provider, model and thinking level

label: resolveSessionSettings has branches for claude, codex and cursor only, so pi and opencode fall to none and the CLI-side prepare record carries no model or effort.
Pi closes that gap from its own extension: liveSettings reads ctx.model.id, ctx.model.provider and getThinkingLevel, and the arm path writes them onto the record.
The OpenCode plugin never reads a model or an effort; its only model access is input.model.limit.context, which sizes the context window.
effort_is_valid has no opencode case, so an OpenCode effort would be rejected even if one were recorded.
append_effort_arguments has cases for claude, codex and pi only, so no OpenCode relaunch ever receives a thinking level.
build_relaunch_arguments drops the model on OpenCode 2 by design because its root command has no model flag, so the receiver starts on the configured default.
Pi's relaunch appends provider, model, thinking level and the plan or build mode, so a Pi hop replays all three carried values.
Neither live run proved the carry: Pi recorded unobservable and OpenCode recorded not-set, and the OpenCode 5/5 came from both sessions sharing the harness default.
live_model_voids_launch_effort deliberately drops the launch effort when the live model differs and brings no usable effort, which is correct and is not the OpenCode gap.

direction: The OpenCode model carries because the plugin reads input.model
reason: It reads only limit.context, a number, and writes nothing to the record.

direction: The Pi carry is broken because resolveSessionSettings has no Pi branch
reason: The Pi extension supplies the values itself, so the missing branch is harmless on Pi.
